[2026-10-11T10:35:57.013Z] [INFO]           "content": "# UX guidelines for the decision screens\n\nThe screens serve one job: an owner or a manager sees what went wrong,\nchecks why, and decides in a minute, without trusting the AI blindly. We did\nnot invent rules for this; we follow the most widely used guidelines for\nhuman-AI interaction, usability and accessibility, and we test each rule as a\nscenario in [`features/14_user_interface.feature`](https://github.com/konard/marketplace-retail-ai-control/blob/main/features/14_user_interface.feature)\nand its neighbours.\n\n## Sources\n\n| Guideline | Why it applies here |\n|---|---|\n| [Microsoft HAX Guidelines for Human-AI Interaction](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/haxtoolkit/ai-guidelines/) (Amershi et al., CHI 2019) — 18 guidelines | the AI proposes, a person decides |\n| [Google People + AI Guidebook](https://pair.withgoogle.com/guidebook/): Explainability + Trust, Feedback + Control, Errors + Graceful Failure | how much to trust an AI explanation |\n| [Nielsen Norman Group, 10 usability heuristics](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/) | the general usability baseline |\n| [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/), level AA | accessibility, also required by public procurement in many countries |\n| [GOV.UK Design System](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/): [error summary](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/error-summary/), [error message](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/error-message/), [details](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/details/) | tested form patterns for people who are not specialists |\n| Ben Shneiderman, [*The Eyes Have It*](https://www.cs.umd.edu/~ben/papers/Shneiderman1996eyes.pdf) (1996): «overview first, zoom and filter, then details on demand» | the order of digest, list, card and evidence |\n| [Pico CSS](https://picocss.com/) | semantic HTML gets readable, accessible styles without our own design system |\n\n## The rules and where they are checked\n\n### 1. Overview first, details on demand\n\nThe morning digest names the 3–5 largest deviations; the home page lists all\nopen ones by money at stake; the card explains one; the evidence page shows\nthe SQL and its rows. Each level links to the next one.\n\n| Screen | Rule | Scenario |\n|---|---|---|\n| Home | sorted by impact, the SKU links to the card | 14 «The home page lists open deviations by impact» |\n| Card | sections in the order a manager asks: what happened → why → what to do → expected effect → decision | 14 «The decision card answers the questions in the order a manager asks them» |\n| Card | the approver's part is one panel; on a wide screen it stays next to the analysis | 14 «What the approver acts on stays together in one decision panel» |\n| Evidence | every figure links to its query (HAX G11, PAIR) | 14 «Every figure can be traced to its data», 05 «Every figure has evidence that links to its SQL query» |\n| Journal | one period, newest first, with a summary line | 15 «By default the journal shows the last four weeks», «The owner reviews one week» |\n\n![The decision card: analysis on the left, decision panel on the right](../screenshots/web-card.png)\n\n### 2. AI output is labelled and its limits are stated\n\n| Guideline | How | Scenario |\n|---|---|---|\n| HAX G1 «Make clear what the system can do» | under the explanation: «Цифры рассчитаны SQL-запросами; AI только объясняет их и предлагает действия в заданных пределах» | 14 «The card says who wrote the explanation» |\n| HAX G2 «Make clear how well the system can do what it can do» | the label «Сгенерировано AI» or «Расчёт по правилам» on every explanation | 14, 05 «The AI model is unavailable» |\n| HAX G11 «Make clear why the system did what it did» | the cause with its numbers and a link to the data | 05 «The margin drop is decomposed by cost item» |\n| PAIR, Errors + Graceful Failure | an AI answer with a figure that is not in the data is never shown; the rules answer instead | 05 «An AI explanation with a figure that is not in the evidence is rejected», 06 «An answer with figures that the data does not back is not shown» |\n| HAX G10 «Scope services when in doubt» | the AI may propose only the actions and the ranges from the settings | 05 «An AI action outside the allowed limits is rejected» |\n\n### 3. The user stays in control\n\n| Guideline | How | Scenario |\n|---|---|---|\n| HAX G9 «Support efficient correction», Nielsen 3 «User control and freedom» | every proposed value is an editable field; an empty field removes the action | 14 «The approver can edit the proposed values before approving», 08 «The approver changes a value before approving» |\n| HAX G8 «Support efficient dismissal» | «Отклонить…» is always one click away, the reason field opens on demand (GOV.UK details) | 14 «What the approver acts on stays together in one decision panel» |\n| HAX G16 «Convey the consequences of user actions» | the panel states the success criterion and when the effect is measured | 14, 10 |\n| Nielsen 1 «Visibility of system status» | every decision shows its status as a word: Ждёт решения, В работе, Цель достигнута, Цель не достигнута | 14 «Accessibility basics on every page», 15 |\n| Nielsen 5 «Error prevention» | only approvers see the buttons; others see why | 14 «A user who is not an approver sees why they cannot decide», 08 |\n\n### 4. Errors are easy to recover from\n\nA rejection without a reason, or a period whose start is after its end, keeps\neverything the user typed and shows the error twice, as GOV.UK does: a\nsummary at the top that links to the field, and the message next to the\nfield (WCAG 3.3.1 Error identification, 3.3.2 Labels or instructions;\nNielsen 9).\n\n| Screen | Scenario |\n|---|---|\n| Card, rejection | 14 «A rejection without a reason shows the error next to the field» |\n| Journal, period | 15 «The start of the period is after its end» |\n| Home, question | 06 |\n\n![The error summary links to the field; the reason is open](../screenshots/web-card-error.png)\n\n### 5. Accessible to everyone (WCAG 2.2 AA)\n\nChecked on every page by 14 «Accessibility basics on every page»:\n\n- 3.1.1 Language of page: `lang=\"ru\"`.\n- 1.3.1 Info and relationships, 4.1.2 Name, role, value: every field has a\n  label; tables have captions and header cells with `scope`.\n- 1.4.1 Use of colour: every status is a word; the colour only repeats it.\n- 2.4.2 Page titled, 1.3.1: one `main` landmark and one `h1`.\n\nDone by construction and checked by review:\n\n- 1.1.1 Non-text content: the sparkline has a text alternative with the\n  first, last and plan values (14 «The decision card answers the questions…»).\n- 2.4.1 Bypass blocks: a «Перейти к содержанию» skip link.\n- 1.4.3 Contrast: status colours are at least 4.5:1 on white.\n- 1.4.10 Reflow: at 320–390 px the layout becomes one column and the menu\n  wraps; nothing scrolls sideways.\n- 2.4.7 Focus visible and keyboard use: plain links, buttons and\n  `<details>`, no custom widgets, no JavaScript.\n\n![The card on a phone, 390 px wide](../screenshots/web-card-mobile.png)\n\n## Reuse instead of a design system\n\n- **Pico CSS** styles semantic HTML: tables, forms, `details`, `article`. Our\n  own CSS is about 50 lines in `src/retail_ai_control/web/static/app.css`:\n  status badges, the two-column card, the error summary.\n- **Server-rendered pages** with Jinja and plain HTML forms. One morning, step by step\n138\t\n139\t`retail-ai-control morning` runs once a day from cron or a systemd timer.\n140\tEvery step is idempotent: a failed source or a failed task is retried on the\n141\tnext run and never stops the other steps.\n142\t\n143\t```mermaid\n144\tsequenceDiagram\n145\t  autonumber\n146\t  participant S as Scheduler\n147\t  participant P as Pilot\n148\t  participant X as WB, Ozon, 1C, CSV\n149\t  participant D as Data mart\n150\t  participant L as LLM\n151\t  participant B as Bitrix24\n152\t\n153\t  S->>P: morning\n154\t  rect rgb(232, 241, 251)\n155\t    P->>X: sync(last N days)\n156\t    X-->>P: sales, ads, stock, cost\n157\t    P->>D: replace the facts of the period\n158\t    P->>D: reconcile with the marketplace reports\n159\t  end\n160\t  rect rgb(234, 245, 236)\n161\t    P->>D: run_followups: decisions whose 7 days have passed\n162\t    D-->>P: margin before and after, control SKUs\n163\t    P->>B: comment on the task with the result\n164\t    P->>D: run_rules: margin, stock, sales, advertising\n165\t  end\n166\t  rect rgb(255, 244, 229)\n167\t    loop every open deviation without a proposal\n168\t      P->>D: evidence queries\n169\t      P->>L: explain and propose, tools = the queries\n170\t      L-->>P: cause, actions\n171\t      P->>P: check numbers and action limits\n172\t      P->>D: proposal with its evidence\n173\t    end\n174\t  end\n175\t  rect rgb(243, 232, 253)\n176\t    P->>B: retry_tasks for approved decisions without a task\n177\t    P->>B: send_digest — the 3–5 largest deviations\n178\t  end\n179\t```\n180\t\n181\tIf the model is not configured, unavailable or returns a number that is not\n182\tin the evidence, the proposal is built by the rules and labelled\n183\t«Расчёт по правилам»; the loop never waits for the AI.\n184\t\n185\t## 4. The life of a decision\n186\t\n187\tA decision is closed only when the follow-up shows that the goal was\n188\tachieved. Otherwise it stays in the journal as evaluated, the deviation is\n189\treopened, and a new proposal links back to it with `parent_id`.\n190\t\n191\t```mermaid\n192\tstateDiagram-v2\n193\t  direction LR\n194\t  classDef wait fill:#fff4e5,stroke:#8a4b00,color:#4a2800\n195\t  classDef work fill:#e8f1fb,stroke:#0b5394,color:#0b2a4a\n196\t  classDef good fill:#eaf5ec,stroke:#1d6b2f,color:#123d1c\n197\t  classDef off fill:#f1f1f1,stroke:#5c5c5c,color:#333333\n198\t\n199\t  [*] --> proposed: deviation found\n200\t  proposed --> approved: approver, with edits\n201\t  proposed --> rejected: approver, with a reason\n202\t  rejected --> [*]: deviation dismissed\n203\t  approved --> in_progress: Bitrix24 task created\n204\t  approved --> approved: task failed, retry next morning\n205\t  in_progress --> done: task completed\n206\t  done --> evaluated: 7 days later, effect measured\n207\t  evaluated --> closed: goal achieved\n208\t  evaluated --> [*]: goal missed, new proposal with parent_id\n209\t  closed --> [*]\n210\t\n211\t  class proposed wait\n212\t  class approved, in_progress, done work\n213\t  class evaluated wait\n214\t  class closed good\n215\t  class rejected off\n216\t```\n217\t\n218\t| Status | Shown as | Who moves it |\n219\t|---|---|---|\n220\t| `proposed` | Ждёт решения | the agent or the rules |\n221\t| `approved` | Утверждено | an approver in the web app |\n222\t| `rejected` | Отклонено | an approver, a reason is required |\n223\t| `in progress` | В работе | the system, when the task is created |\n224\t| `done` | Выполнено, ждём эффект | Bitrix24 task event |\n225\t| `evaluated` | Цель не достигнута | follow-up, goal missed or partly achieved |\n226\t| `closed` | Цель достигнута | follow-up, goal achieved |\n227\t\n228\t## 5. One morning, step by step\n\n`retail-ai-control morning` runs once a day from cron or a systemd timer.\nEvery step is idempotent: a failed source or a failed task is retried on the\nnext run and never stops the other steps.\n\n```mermaid\nsequenceDiagram\n  autonumber\n  participant S as Scheduler\n  participant P as Pilot\n  participant X as WB, Ozon, 1C, CSV\n  participant D as Data mart\n  participant L as LLM\n  participant B as Bitrix24\n\n  S->>P: morning\n  rect rgb(232, 241, 251)\n    P->>X: sync(last N days)\n    X-->>P: sales, ads, stock, cost\n    P->>D: replace the facts of the period\n    P->>D: reconcile with the marketplace reports\n  end\n  rect rgb(234, 245, 236)\n    P->>D: run_followups: decisions whose 7 days have passed\n    D-->>P: margin before and after, control SKUs\n    P->>B: comment on the task with the result\n    P->>D: run_rules: margin, stock, sales, advertising\n  end\n  rect rgb(255, 244, 229)\n    loop every open deviation without a proposal\n      P->>D: evidence queries\n      P->>L: explain and propose, tools = the queries\n      L-->>P: cause, actions\n      P->>P: check numbers and action limits\n      P->>D: proposal with its evidence\n    end\n  end\n  rect rgb(243, 232, 253)\n    P->>B: retry_tasks for approved decisions without a task\n    P->>B: send_digest — the 3–5 largest deviations\n  end\n```\n\nIf the model is not configured, unavailable or returns a number that is not\nin the evidence, the proposal is built by the rules and labelled\n«Расчёт по правилам»; the loop never waits for the AI.\n\n## 4. The life of a decision\n\nA decision is closed only when the follow-up shows that the goal was\nachieved. Otherwise it stays in the journal as evaluated, the deviation is\nreopened, and a new proposal links back to it with `parent_id`.\n\n```mermaid\nstateDiagram-v2\n  direction LR\n  classDef wait fill:#fff4e5,stroke:#8a4b00,color:#4a2800\n  classDef work fill:#e8f1fb,stroke:#0b5394,color:#0b2a4a\n  classDef good fill:#eaf5ec,stroke:#1d6b2f,color:#123d1c\n  classDef off fill:#f1f1f1,stroke:#5c5c5c,color:#333333\n\n  [*] --> proposed: deviation found\n  proposed --> approved: approver, with edits\n  proposed --> rejected: approver, with a reason\n  rejected --> [*]: deviation dismissed\n  approved --> in_progress: Bitrix24 task created\n  approved --> approved: task failed, retry next morning\n  in_progress --> done: task completed\n  done --> evaluated: 7 days later, effect measured\n  evaluated --> closed: goal achieved\n  evaluated --> [*]: goal missed, new proposal with parent_id\n  closed --> [*]\n\n  class proposed wait\n  class approved, in_progress, done work\n  class evaluated wait\n  class closed good\n  class rejected off\n```\n\n| Status | Shown as | Who moves it |\n|---|---|---|\n| `proposed` | Ждёт решения | the agent or the rules |\n| `approved` | Утверждено | an approver in the web app |\n| `rejected` | Отклонено | an approver, a reason is required |\n| `in progress` | В работе | the system, when the task is created |\n| `done` | Выполнено, ждём эффект | Bitrix24 task event |\n| `evaluated` | Цель не достигнута | follow-up, goal missed or partly achieved |\n| `closed` | Цель достигнута | follow-up, goal achieved |\n\n## 5. Data mart\n\nAll figures come from SQL over these tables; the AI reads them through the\nsame queries and cannot write.\n\n```mermaid\nerDiagram\n  product ||--o{ cost_price : \"priced from 1C\"\n  product ||--o{ sales_daily : \"sold\"\n  product ||--o{ ad_spend_daily : \"advertised\"\n  product ||--o{ stock_daily : \"stocked\"\n  product ||--o{ deviation : \"deviates\"\n  deviation ||--o{ evidence : \"proved by\"\n  deviation ||--o{ decision : \"answered by\"\n  decision ||--o{ decision_event : \"journal\"\n  decision |o--o{ decision : \"parent_id\"\n\n  product {\n    string sku PK\n    string wb_nm_id\n    string ozon_sku\n  }\n  sales_daily {\n    string channel PK\n    string sku PK\n    date day PK\n    int units\n    money revenue\n    money commission\n    money logistics\n  }\n  deviation {\n    int id PK\n    string rule\n    string sku\n    string channel\n    money impact\n    string status\n  }\n  evidence {\n    int id PK\n    string name\n    text sql\n    json rows\n  }\n  decision {\n    int id PK\n    int deviation_id FK\n    int parent_id FK\n    string status\n    json actions\n    string task_id\n    string outcome\n    money incremental_margin\n  }\n  decision_event {\n    int id PK\n    int decision_id FK\n    string stage\n    date on_day\n  }\n```\n\nSupport tables: `reconciliation` (computed vs reported revenue per channel and\nweek), `unmapped` (marketplace items without a 1C SKU) and `sync_run` (one row\nper source and run). Sources and verification notes are in\n[docs/concept/sources.md](docs/concept/sources.md).\n\nThe concept answers [issue #1](https://github.com/konard/marketplace-retail-ai-control/issues/1).\nIt describes one management loop, monitoring → analysis → decision →\nexecution → follow-up, for sales, profitability, costs and team performance.\nThe repository also holds the pilot from the concept: an executable\nspecification in Gherkin and a small Python implementation that passes it.\n\n| Document | What is in it |\n|---|---|\n| [Concept](docs/concept/README.md) | two reference examples, the proposal, the pilot (Russian) |\n| [Executable specification](features/README.md) | 16 features; every scenario is an automated test |\n| [Architecture](docs/architecture/README.md) | context, modules, one morning, the life of a decision, data mart, deployment |\n| [UX guidelines](docs/ux/README.md) | HAX, People + AI, NN/g, GOV.UK and WCAG 2.2 rules mapped to the scenarios that test them |\n\n![The decision card: what happened, why, what to do, and the decision panel](docs/screenshots/web-card.png)\n\n## Features\n\n- **Concept.** Two sourced reference examples (Shopify Sidekick + Flow with\n  the SNOCKS case; Bitrix24 BI Конструктор + BitrixGPT + robots), a\n  build-vs-buy split, one end-to-end scenario and a 6–8 week pilot with a\n  success metric, the main risk and open questions.\n- **Specification first.** Every behaviour is a scenario in\n  [`features/`](features/README.md), written before the code and run by\n  [pytest-bdd](https://pytest-bdd.readthedocs.io/). The traceability table in\n  `features/README.md` links each part of the concept to its feature.\n- **The loop, implemented** in `src/retail_ai_control/`:\n  - data from Wildberries, Ozon, 1C (OData) and an analytics CSV export into\n    one mart, with SKU mapping and reconciliation against marketplace reports;\n  - unit economics per SKU × channel × day and deviation rules for margin,\n    advertising share, sales drop and stock cover;\n  - an AI explanation and proposal built only from SQL evidence; an answer\n    with an unsupported figure or an action outside the limits is replaced\n    by a rule-based one;\n  - a morning digest in the Bitrix24 chat, approval with edits or rejection\n    with a reason, a Bitrix24 task with a checklist and a deadline;\n  - a follow-up after 7 days against control SKUs: the decision is closed\n    when the goal is achieved, otherwise a new proposal is made;\n  - the decision journal, team results and the pilot scorecard.\n- **Web app** for the decisions: server-rendered pages with FastAPI, Jinja\n  and Pico CSS, no JavaScript, WCAG 2.2 AA basics tested on every page.\n- **Ready parts instead of custom code:** httpx, SQLAlchemy Core, the\n  OpenAI-compatible client (GigaChat, YandexGPT or a local model), Metabase\n  alerts, Bitrix24 REST.\n\n## Quick Start\n\n```bash\npython -m venv .venv\nsource .venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: .venv\\Scripts\\activate\npip install -e \".[dev,docs]\"\n```\n\nSee every screen on demo data, without connecting any system:\n\n```bash\nretail-ai-control --config examples/pilot.toml demo\nretail-ai-control --config examples/pilot.toml serve --user 1\n# open http://127.0.0.1:8000\n```\n\nThe commands of the loop:\n\n| Command | What it does |\n|---|---|\n| `retail-ai-control sync --from 2026-10-01 --to 2026-10-07` | load the sources for a date range |\n| `retail-ai-control morning` | sync, reconcile, measure due effects, find deviations, propose, send the digest; run it daily from a systemd timer or cron |\n| `retail-ai-control followup` | retry failed tasks and measure due effects |\n| `retail-ai-control ask \"почему упала маржа на Ozon?\"` | ask a question about the data |\n| `retail-ai-control serve` | the web app and the Metabase and Bitrix24 webhooks |\n\nAdd `--verbose` to log every step.\n\nRun the specification, the tests and the same checks as CI:\n\n```bash\npytest tests/bdd            # the Gherkin scenarios only\npytest                      # everything\nruff check . && ruff format --check . && mypy src tests/bdd\npython scripts/check_file_size.py\nbash scripts/check-required-docs.sh\nsphinx-build -W --keep-going -b html docs _site\n```\n\nTo check that the concept fits on two A4 pages, render it to PDF. This\nrequires Playwright and Chromium:\n\n```bash\npip install playwright markdown && playwright install chromium\npython experiments/render_concept_pdf.py\n```\n\n## Configuration\n\nThe pilot reads one TOML file: `--config`, `$RETAIL_AI_CONTROL_CONFIG` or\n`pilot.toml`. [`examples/pilot.toml`](examples/pilot.toml) lists every\nsetting: rule thresholds, action limits, margin plans, approvers and the\nmanager of each channel. Tokens and passwords come only from environment\nvariables:\n\n| Variable | Used for |\n|---|---|\n| `RETAIL_AI_WB_TOKEN` | Wildberries API |\n| `RETAIL_AI_OZON_API_KEY` | Ozon Seller API |\n| `RETAIL_AI_ONEC_PASSWORD` | 1C OData |\n| `RETAIL_AI_LLM_API_KEY` | the OpenAI-compatible LLM API |\n| `RETAIL_AI_BITRIX_WEBHOOK_URL` | Bitrix24 REST: chat and tasks |\n| `RETAIL_AI_BITRIX_APPLICATION_TOKEN` | checks Bitrix24 task events |\n| `RETAIL_AI_METABASE_SECRET` | checks Metabase alerts |\n\nWithout an LLM key the loop runs on rules and labels its proposals\n«Расчёт по правилам».\n\n| Path | Purpose |\n|---|---|\n| `docs/concept/` | the concept (Russian, at most 2 pages) and its sources |\n| `docs/architecture/`, `docs/ux/`, `docs/screenshots/` | architecture, UX guidelines, screenshots of every screen |\n| `features/` | the executable specification |\n| `src/retail_ai_control/` | the implementation |\n| `tests/bdd/` | step definitions; `tests/test_concept_doc.py` checks the concept |\n| `docs/preview-regeneration.md` | template note on preview regeneration (inherited) |\n\n### Deploying API documentation\n\nThe `Docs` workflow (`.github/workflows/docs.yml`) builds the Sphinx site,\nincluding the concept, on every push and pull request. It publishes the site\nto GitHub Pages on `main` only when two things are set up:\n\n- `Settings -> Pages -> Source` is set to `GitHub Actions`.\n- The repository variable `DEPLOY_GITHUB_PAGES` is set to `true`.\n\nThe repository is based on the\n[python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template).\nIts CI/CD pipeline covers lint, tests, docs, links, security and workflow\naudit. Its example package `src/my_package` is kept so those checks keep\nrunning.\n\n## Contributing\n\nSee [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).\n\n- Change a scenario in `features/` first, see it fail, then change the code.\n- Changes under `src/`, `tests/` or `scripts/` need a fragment in\n  `changelog.d/`.\n- Run the checks from [Quick Start](#quick-start) before you push.\n- Keep the concept in Russian and within 2 pages; use Mermaid for diagrams\n  and store images as files next to the document.\n\n## License\n\n[Unlicense](LICENSE) - Public Domain\n"

Sources and verification notes are in\n[docs/concept/sources.md](docs/concept/sources.md).\n\nThe concept answers [issue #1](https://github.com/konard/marketplace-retail-ai-control/issues/1).\nIt describes one management loop, monitoring → analysis → decision →\nexecution → follow-up, for sales, profitability, costs and team performance.\nThe repository also holds the pilot from the concept: an executable\nspecification in Gherkin and a small Python implementation that passes it.\n\n| Document | What is in it |\n|---|---|\n| [Concept](docs/concept/README.md) | two reference examples, the proposal, the pilot (Russian) |\n| [Executable specification](features/README.md) | 16 features; every scenario is an automated test |\n| [Architecture](docs/architecture/README.md) | context, modules, one morning, the life of a decision, data mart, deployment |\n| [UX guidelines](docs/ux/README.md) | HAX, People + AI, NN/g, GOV.UK and WCAG 2.2 rules mapped to the scenarios that test them |\n\n![The decision card: what happened, why, what to do, and the decision panel](docs/screenshots/web-card.png)\n\n## Features\n\n- **Concept.** Two sourced reference examples (Shopify Sidekick + Flow with\n  the SNOCKS case; Bitrix24 BI Конструктор + BitrixGPT + robots), a\n  build-vs-buy split, one end-to-end scenario and a 6–8 week pilot with a\n  success metric, the main risk and open questions.\n- **Specification first.** Every behaviour is a scenario in\n  [`features/`](features/README.md), written before the code and run by\n  [pytest-bdd](https://pytest-bdd.readthedocs.io/). The traceability table in\n  `features/README.md` links each part of the concept to its feature.\n- **The loop, implemented** in `src/retail_ai_control/`:\n  - data from Wildberries, Ozon, 1C (OData) and an analytics CSV export into\n    one mart, with SKU mapping and reconciliation against marketplace reports;\n  - unit economics per SKU × channel × day and deviation rules for margin,\n    advertising share, sales drop and stock cover;\n  - an AI explanation and proposal built only from SQL evidence; an answer\n    with an unsupported figure or an action outside the limits is replaced\n    by a rule-based one;\n  - a morning digest in the Bitrix24 chat, approval with edits or rejection\n    with a reason, a Bitrix24 task with a checklist and a deadline;\n  - a follow-up after 7 days against control SKUs: the decision is closed\n    when the goal is achieved, otherwise a new proposal is made;\n  - the decision journal, team results and the pilot scorecard.\n- **Web app** for the decisions: server-rendered pages with FastAPI, Jinja\n  and Pico CSS, no JavaScript, WCAG 2.2 AA basics tested on every page.\n- **Ready parts instead of custom code:** httpx, SQLAlchemy Core, the\n  OpenAI-compatible client (GigaChat, YandexGPT or a local model), Metabase\n  alerts, Bitrix24 REST.\n\n## Quick Start\n\n```bash\npython -m venv .venv\nsource .venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: .venv\\Scripts\\activate\npip install -e \".[dev,docs]\"\n```\n\nSee every screen on demo data, without connecting any system:\n\n```bash\nretail-ai-control --config examples/pilot.toml demo\nretail-ai-control --config examples/pilot.toml serve --user 1\n# open http://127.0.0.1:8000\n```\n\nThe commands of the loop:\n\n| Command | What it does |\n|---|---|\n| `retail-ai-control sync --from 2026-10-01 --to 2026-10-07` | load the sources for a date range |\n| `retail-ai-control morning` | sync, reconcile, measure due effects, find deviations, propose, send the digest; run it daily from a systemd timer or cron |\n| `retail-ai-control followup` | retry failed tasks and measure due effects |\n| `retail-ai-control ask \"почему упала маржа на Ozon?\"` | ask a question about the data |\n| `retail-ai-control serve` | the web app and the Metabase and Bitrix24 webhooks |\n\nAdd `--verbose` to log every step.\n\nRun the specification, the tests and the same checks as CI:\n\n```bash\npytest tests/bdd            # the Gherkin scenarios only\npytest                      # everything\nruff check . && ruff format --check . && mypy src tests/bdd\npython scripts/check_file_size.py\nbash scripts/check-required-docs.sh\nsphinx-build -W --keep-going -b html docs _site\n```\n\nTo check that the concept fits on two A4 pages, render it to PDF. a build-vs-buy split;\n  - daily use by the owner, managers and employees;\n  - one end-to-end scenario: detect → suggest a fix → a person approves →\n    the task is completed → the outcome is checked;\n  - a 6–8 week pilot with a success metric, the main risk and open questions.\n- **Stack:** Python connectors to 1C, Bitrix24 and the marketplace APIs →\n  PostgreSQL → Metabase alerts → an LLM agent with tool calling → tasks\n  created through the Bitrix24 task API.\n- **Automated checks** keep the concept in shape: required sections, Mermaid\n  diagrams, image files next to the document, the length budget, and a README\n  that links to the result first.\n\n## Quick Start\n\nRead the result on GitHub: [docs/concept/README.md](docs/concept/README.md).\nGitHub renders the Mermaid diagrams inline.\n\nTo build the documentation site locally (Sphinx + MyST + Mermaid):\n\n```bash\npython -m venv .venv\nsource .venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: .venv\\Scripts\\activate\npip install -e \".[dev,docs]\"\n\nsphinx-build -W --keep-going -b html docs _site\n```\n\nTo run the same checks as CI:\n\n```bash\nruff check . && ruff format --check . && mypy src/\npython scripts/check_file_size.py\nbash scripts/check-required-docs.sh\npytest\n```\n\nTo check that the concept fits on two A4 pages, render it to PDF. External systems (WB, Ozon, 1C, Bitrix24, the LLM) are faked at the HTTP level, so the production code runs unchanged.\n\n| Concept: loop stage / pilot item | Feature |\n|---|---|\n| Data from 1C, WB, Ozon and the analytics export into one mart | \\`01_data_collection\\` |\n| Unit economics per SKU × channel × day | \\`02_unit_economics\\` |\n| Main risk, wrong numbers: reconciliation (≤2%) | \\`03_reconciliation\\` |\n| Monitoring: deviation rules | \\`04_deviation_detection\\` |\n| AI: cause, proposal, evidence for every figure, action limits | \\`05_ai_analysis\\` |\n| Questions in plain language | \\`06_questions\\` |\n| Morning digest in the Bitrix24 chat | \\`07_daily_digest\\` |\n| Approve / edit / reject with a reason | \\`08_decision_approval\\` |\n| Bitrix24 task with checklist, deadline, criterion; retry on failure | \\`09_task_execution\\` |\n| Follow-up after 7 days against control SKUs | \\`10_follow_up\\` |\n| Team performance | \\`11_team_performance\\` |\n| Pilot scorecard: incremental margin, approval rate, lead time | \\`12_pilot_scorecard\\` |\n| The whole scenario from the concept, end to end | \\`13_end_to_end\\` |\n| Web UI and accessibility | \\`14_user_interface\\` |\n| Decision journal | \\`15_decision_journal\\` |\n| Demo data | \\`16_demo\\` |\n\n## Implementation: ready libraries, little custom code\n\n\\`src/retail_ai_control/\\` is the thin Python layer from the concept. It also has a table linking each part of the concept to its feature.\n- WB, Ozon, 1C, Bitrix24 and the LLM are faked at the HTTP level, so the real code runs unchanged in the tests.\n\n**Implementation**\n- `src/retail_ai_control/` covers the whole loop:\n  - connectors;\n  - a data mart with unit economics per SKU, channel and day;\n  - deviation rules;\n  - an AI step that checks every figure against SQL, and falls back to a rule-based proposal labelled «Расчёт по правилам»;\n  - the Bitrix24 digest and tasks;\n  - the 7-day follow-up;\n  - the decision journal, team results and the pilot scorecard;\n  - a web app, a CLI and a `demo` command.\n- To keep the code small it reuses ready libraries: httpx, SQLAlchemy Core, FastAPI with Jinja and Pico CSS, an OpenAI-compatible client, Metabase alerts and Bitrix24 REST.\n\n**UX guidelines** (`docs/ux/README.md`)\n- The rules come from Microsoft HAX, Google People + AI, the Nielsen Norman Group heuristics, GOV.UK form patterns and WCAG 2.2 AA.\n- Each rule is mapped to the scenario that tests it.\n- Screenshots of every screen are in `docs/screenshots/` and embedded in the PR description.\n\n**Diagrams** (`docs/architecture/README.md`)\n- There are six styled Mermaid diagrams and a legend: system context, containers and modules, one morning step by step, the life of a decision, the data mart, and deployment.\n- Wide diagrams on the docs site used to be squeezed into a fixed 500 px box. A docs config change lets each one keep its own size and uses a neutral theme.\n- All 10 diagrams, including the 3 in the concept, render without errors; I checked each one in a browser.\n\n**Last step**\n- I rewrote the README to describe the documents, the commands and the environment variables. While checking it, I corrected one wrong claim: the AI step is switched on by setting `[llm] base_url`, not by providing an API key.\n- I also updated the changelog entry and the PR title and description.\n- Locally, everything passed: ruff, mypy, the file-size and required-docs checks, `pytest` (486 passed, 1 skipped) and the strict docs build."

The deliverable is a two-page concept, written in Russian, for an AI management loop at a Wildberries/Ozon retailer that uses 1C and Bitrix24:\n\n**[docs/concept/README.md](https://github.com/konard/marketplace-retail-ai-control/blob/issue-1-591af66fa54f/docs/concept/README.md)**\n\nFollowing the review request, the pilot from the concept is now also an **executable specification** and a **working implementation** of it. The pilot comes with an architecture document with styled diagrams, UX guidelines that come from the most widely used sources, and a demo of every screen.\n\n| Document | What is in it |\n|---|---|\n| [Concept](https://github.com/konard/marketplace-retail-ai-control/blob/issue-1-591af66fa54f/docs/concept/README.md) + [sources](https://github.com/konard/marketplace-retail-ai-control/blob/issue-1-591af66fa54f/docs/concept/sources.md) | two reference examples, the proposal, the pilot (Russian, 2 A4 pages) |\n| [Executable specification](https://github.com/konard/marketplace-retail-ai-control/blob/issue-1-591af66fa54f/features/README.md) | 16 Gherkin features, 86 scenarios (105 test cases with outline examples), traceability to the concept |\n| [Architecture](https://github.com/konard/marketplace-retail-ai-control/blob/issue-1-591af66fa54f/docs/architecture/README.md) | context (C4 L1), containers and modules, one morning (sequence), the life of a decision (state), data mart (ER), deployment |\n| [UX guidelines](https://github.com/konard/marketplace-retail-ai-control/blob/issue-1-591af66fa54f/docs/ux/README.md) | Microsoft HAX, Google People + AI, NN/g heuristics, GOV.UK patterns and WCAG 2.2 AA, each rule mapped to the scenario that tests it |\n\n## The concept (unchanged in substance)\n\n- **Part 1. Two reference examples**, each with a loop diagram, a screenshot, what to adopt, its limits, and where the knowledge comes from:\n  1. Shopify Sidekick + Flow, with the SNOCKS case study;\n  2. Bitrix24 BI Конструктор + BitrixGPT + robots.\n- **Part 2. Proposal:**\n  - the architecture;\n  - a build-vs-buy table;\n  - how the owner and the employees use it day to day;\n  - one end-to-end scenario;\n  - a 6–8 week pilot with a metric, the main risk and open questions.\n\n![Concept render](https://github.com/konard/marketplace-retail-ai-control/blob/issue-1-591af66fa54f/docs/screenshots/concept-render.png?raw=true)\n\n## Specification first: Cucumber/Gherkin + TDD on every scenario\n\nEvery user scenario is a Gherkin scenario in `features/`, run by [pytest-bdd](https://pytest-bdd.readthedocs.io/). The workflow is in [features/README.md](https://github.com/konard/marketplace-retail-ai-control/blob/issue-1-591af66fa54f/features/README.md): change the scenario, see it fail, then change the code. External systems (WB, Ozon, 1C, Bitrix24, the LLM) are faked at the HTTP level, so the production code runs unchanged.\n\n| Concept: loop stage / pilot item | Feature |\n|---|---|\n| Data from 1C, WB, Ozon and the analytics export into one mart | `01_data_collection` |\n| Unit economics per SKU × channel × day | `02_unit_economics` |\n| Main risk, wrong numbers: reconciliation (≤2%) | `03_reconciliation` |\n| Monitoring: deviation rules | `04_deviation_detection` |\n| AI: cause, proposal, evidence for every figure, action limits | `05_ai_analysis` |\n| Questions in plain language | `06_questions` |\n| Morning digest in the Bitrix24 chat | `07_daily_digest` |\n| Approve / edit / reject with a reason | `08_decision_approval` |\n| Bitrix24 task with checklist, deadline, criterion; retry on failure | `09_task_execution` |\n| Follow-up after 7 days against control SKUs | `10_follow_up` |\n| Team performance | `11_team_performance` |\n| Pilot scorecard: incremental margin, approval rate, lead time | `12_pilot_scorecard` |\n| The whole scenario from the concept, end to end | `13_end_to_end` |\n| Web UI and accessibility | `14_user_interface` |\n| Decision journal | `15_decision_journal` |\n| Demo data | `16_demo` |\n\n## Implementation: ready libraries, little custom code\n\n`src/retail_ai_control/` is the thin Python layer from the concept. Ready parts do the rest:\n\n- httpx for the connectors;\n- SQLAlchemy Core with SQLite or PostgreSQL;\n- an OpenAI-compatible client (GigaChat, YandexGPT or a local model);\n- Metabase alerts;\n- Bitrix24 REST (`im.message.add`, `tasks.task.add`, task events);\n- FastAPI + Jinja + Pico CSS for the server-rendered web app, with no JavaScript.\n\nWhat the code guarantees:\n\n- Numbers come only from SQL. An AI answer with an unsupported figure, or with an action outside the configured limits, is replaced by a rule-based proposal labelled «Расчёт по правилам».\n- Tokens come only from environment variables.\n\n## UX\n\nThe screens follow «overview first, details on demand»: digest → list → decision card → evidence. The AI text is labelled and its limits are stated. A person always decides, and every rejection needs a reason. Errors use the GOV.UK error summary pattern. Each rule is tested on every page, including:\n\n- WCAG 2.2 AA basics: landmarks, labels, focus, contrast, and reflow on a phone.\n\n| Decision card | Error summary | Phone (reflow) |\n|---|---|---|\n| ![card](https://github.com/konard/marketplace-retail-ai-control/blob/issue-1-591af66fa54f/docs/screenshots/web-card.png?raw=true) | ![error](https://github.com/konard/marketplace-retail-ai-control/blob/issue-1-591af66fa54f/docs/screenshots/web-card-error.png?raw=true) | ![mobile](https://github.com/konard/marketplace-retail-ai-control/blob/issue-1-591af66fa54f/docs/screenshots/web-card-mobile.png?raw=true) |\n\n| Home: what needs attention | Decision journal | Team | Pilot scorecard |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| ![home](https://github.com/konard/marketplace-retail-ai-control/blob/issue-1-591af66fa54f/docs/screenshots/web-home.png?raw=true) | ![journal](https://github.com/konard/marketplace-retail-ai-control/blob/issue-1-591af66fa54f/docs/screenshots/web-journal.png?raw=true) | ![team](https://github.com/konard/marketplace-retail-ai-control/blob/issue-1-591af66fa54f/docs/screenshots/web-team.png?raw=true) | ![scorecard](https://github.com/konard/marketplace-retail-ai-control/blob/issue-1-591af66fa54f/docs/screenshots/web-scorecard.png?raw=true) |\n\n## Diagrams\n\nAll diagrams are Mermaid, so GitHub and the Sphinx site render them from text. The architecture uses one legend and one colour per role. The C4-style context draws the whole system as one box. The Sphinx config now uses `mermaid_height = \"auto\"` and the neutral theme, so wide diagrams are no longer squeezed into a fixed 500 px box. The three concept diagrams use the same colour per loop stage.\n\n## Try it\n\n```bash\npip install -e \".[dev,docs]\"\nretail-ai-control --config examples/pilot.toml demo\nretail-ai-control --config examples/pilot.toml serve --user 1   # http://127.0.0.1:8000\npytest tests/bdd                                                 # the specification\n```\n\n## Other changes\n\n- **README.md:** describes the documents, the features, the commands and the environment variables. It still links to the concept first.\n- **`tests/test_concept_doc.py` and `experiments/render_concept_pdf.py`:** check the concept's structure, links, word budget and the 2-page A4 limit.\n- **CI fix, Security → Dependency Review:**\n  - The problem: the repository's Dependency graph is off, so the review failed every PR with \"Dependency review is not supported on this repository\".\n  - The fix: `scripts/check-dependency-graph.sh` probes the SBOM endpoint and skips the review with a warning only on 404. Any other answer still runs the review.\n  - Tests: `tests/test_check_dependency_graph.py`.\n- **Changelog fragment:** `changelog.d/20261010_issue_1_concept.md`.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- **WB and Ozon API docs:** these returned anti-bot or geo pages (498/403) from the research environment, so they are mentioned without links.\n- **The tante-e test:** it returns a persistent Cloudflare 429 to every non-browser client, so it is cited as text in the appendix. `.lycheeignore` stays empty.\n- **Numbers:** all numbers in the scenarios and the demo are illustrative.\n- **Scope of the implementation:** it is a pilot, deliberately kept simple for the requirements refinement that follows.
